title: Extinct Animals, Fossils & Evolution
source: Science G3 B1 Study sheet pp.16-19, Worksheet Q12-Q13

scenes.t: An animal is endangered when its numbers go down quickly. Tigers, pandas, rhinos and turtles are endangered. We must take care of them!
An animal is extinct when all of its kind have died and none is alive on Earth. Dinosaurs, dodo birds, mammoths and saber-tooth cats are extinct.
Lonesome George was a tortoise. He was the last one of his kind, so he was lonely.
Humans brought goats to his island. The goats ate all the food, so the tortoises could not eat and many died.
Scientists took care of George, but when he died, his kind became extinct. Humans can harm the environment, but we can also protect it.
How do we know about animals from long ago? From fossils! Fossils are the remains of living things from a long time ago, found in rocks.
Evolution is how living things slowly change over a very long time. Archaeopteryx had wings, feathers and a beak like a bird, but teeth, fingers and claws like a dinosaur.

why.x: None of its kind is alive today.
why.e: It is still alive, but very few are left.

activities.title: Make Your Own Fossil
activities.goal: Make a fossil print like the ones scientists find in rocks.
need: a shell, a leaf or a toy dinosaur
a rolling pin or a cup

predict.q: What will you see when you lift the shell?
o: Its shape printed in the dough

steps.t: Roll the dough flat and smooth.
Press the shell or leaf firmly into the dough.
Leave the dough to dry for one day. Now you have a fossil!

activities.result: The exact shape and lines of the shell stay printed in the dough.
activities.why: Long ago, plants and animals were pressed into mud. Over a very long time the mud turned into rock and kept their shapes as fossils.
